title: CSS Grid
subtitle: Create powerful two-dimensional website layouts using CSS Grid.
description: Learn rows, columns, gaps, grid areas and responsive layouts for building complex page structures.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 7: CSS Grid. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “CSS Grid”. The goal is to create powerful two-dimensional website layouts using CSS Grid.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

CSS Grid manages rows and columns together, which makes it useful for card collections, dashboards, and page-level layout. Define tracks with grid-template-columns or grid-template-rows and use gap for consistent spacing.

blocks.question: A card grid should create as many columns as fit without horizontal overflow. What is a useful pattern?
options: Set every card to a fixed 900px width.
Use table layout for the page.
Use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(..., 1fr)) with a reasonable minimum.
blocks.explanation: Auto-fit with minmax allows the column count to respond to available space.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Auto-fit with minmax allows the column count to respond to available space.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Auto-fit with minmax allows the column count to respond to available space.

blocks.text: Flexible units such as fr distribute remaining space, while minmax and repeat can create layouts that adapt to available width. Do not force a fixed number of columns if the screen may be narrow.

blocks.question: A program repeatedly looks up a learner by a unique email address. Which structure is a natural fit?
options: A map/dictionary keyed by email, with suitable uniqueness handling.
A random number with no mapping.
A paragraph of comma-separated values that is never parsed.
A loop that guesses the correct person.
blocks.explanation: Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
